people.gloss: The blue luan bird, messenger of the immortals
people.role: A founder (1110) and head of Bách Vũ Các; raises the palace's post birds and gathers the feathers for its fans
people.appearance: A quick, bright-eyed woman in a cloak of moulted feathers, with three small birds asleep along her shoulders and a bone whistle on a cord.
people.backstory: Tạ Thanh Loan grew up netting birds with her sister Tạ Thanh Thước (ta_thanh_thuoc) in the cinnamon woods of Nhục Quế Thôn, under an old catcher, Tuyên Bách Minh (tuyen_bach_minh), who told them all birds bow to the phoenix. In 1110 the three of them founded the pavilion to raise messenger birds for the palace (V137). Tuyên would not lead, so she did. The pavilion's birds now carry the palace's ordinary post, its fan-makers supply the inner gate, and its catchers bring down the vent-bird feathers for the Feather Kindling. The palace's writs still fly on the red-crested birds of the Wutong Court, which Vu Ngô Đồng (vu_ngo_dong) keeps and lends her and never asks back. In 1180 she sent her nephew Ổ Linh Tước (o_linh_tuoc) to the Wutong Court to learn them, and since 1196 he has sent their eggs home. In 1199 the last basket came down lined with the Court hen's plucked down, and she burned it before her sister could see. She is 128 and Trúc Cơ.
people.wants: The palace's writs carried on the pavilion's birds, and the pavilion counted among the palace's halls rather than its servants.
people.secret: In a hidden loft she has nine red-crested writ birds, hatched from eggs her nephew carried out of the Wutong aviary without Vu Ngô Đồng's leave. In 1199 he wrung the neck of the Court's breeding hen to take the last clutch, and the basket came lined with the hen's down; Tạ burned it and told her sister the eggs were Vu's gift. She is taking the nine to the Fire Court anyway, and she has promised Ổ the writ loft for his silence, over the girl who raised the birds.

people.role: Co-founder; keeper of the moulting lofts, where the hundred feathers are gathered
people.appearance: A stooped, soft-voiced woman with feathers in her hair she has forgotten are there.
people.backstory: The elder Tạ sister, Tạ Thanh Thước keeps the lofts where the pavilion's birds moult and gathers every shed feather by kind. She has ninety-nine kinds in her fan and an empty socket for the hundredth. Her husband Ổ Tùng Lâm (o_tung_lam) was killed by the dark apes of Huyền Viên Lâm in 1168. She believes the red-crested eggs her son Ổ Linh Tước (o_linh_tuoc) sends home are Vu Ngô Đồng's gift.
people.wants: The hundredth feather for her fan, and her son home to see the socket filled.
people.secret: In the dark of each moon she sells her duplicate feathers by kind to the fan-maker Hàng Thải Vũ, to pay a stone-cutter for a marker for Ổ Tùng Lâm, whom the apes never gave back.

people.role: Master of the post birds; flies the palace's ordinary letters
people.appearance: A wiry, grinning man with bird droppings on both shoulders and a dozen seal impressions in his memory.
people.backstory: Born at Hà Loan the year the pavilion was founded, Giải Vân Tiêu trains and flies the post birds that carry the palace's ordinary letters to every vassal. He knows every seal by sight. For forty years the palace's guest elder Chử Trì Âm (chu_tri_am) has sent letters north by his birds to Thính Vũ Lâu, and Giải has noticed that the replies come back with a second seal under the first. He has told only Tạ Thanh Loan (ta_thanh_loan), and she told him to forget it. Since the head told him to forget it, he has begun to open and reseal them.
people.wants: A post-house of his own in Hà Loan with a roof of birds, and every seal on the road one he can read.
people.secret: He opens the second-sealed letters, copies the seal into a wax tablet, and closes them again with a spoon-heated knife; Chử Trì Âm has not yet noticed the replies arriving a day late.

people.role: Fan-maker; supplies Phượng Minh's inner gate with practice fans
people.backstory: A peach farmer's daughter from Đào Khê who makes every practice fan the palace's inner gate burns through, and complains to its fan master Thích Hồng Linh (thich_hong_linh) that they burn them too fast. She returned a whole bundle of Kỷ Hồng Phiến's (ky_hong_phien) binding for one crooked rib and passed the next bundle unseen, and Kỷ paid for the first from her own wage.
people.appearance: Rows of old burn blisters along both forearms, one per inner-gate season.

people.role: Outer catcher of the jungle; father of Trần Tước Nhi at the Wutong Court
people.backstory: A lime-stick catcher who never passed to the inner gate and sent his daughter Trần Tước Nhi (tran_tuoc_nhi) to the palace's aviary instead; she names every chick and writes him their names. He sleeps in the shade while his lime-sticks dry.

ties.note: his daughter, aviary girl of the Wutong Court

people.role: The head's inner disciple; keeps the hidden loft
people.backstory: Tạ Thanh Loan (ta_thanh_loan) gave her the key to a loft no one else may enter and nine red-crested birds to feed, and she is sure it is an honour. Every dawn she teaches them to come to her master's whistle and roost in that loft, because no one has told her a gift should home anywhere else.
people.appearance: A whistle's red dent in her lower lip.

people.role: Outer disciple; sings the birds in
people.backstory: A cinnamon picker's girl who sings the post birds home at dusk; when every bird on the ridge fell silent in 1195 (A248), hers stopped too, and Tạ Thanh Loan (ta_thanh_loan) asked her for the tune. When the fledgling Nhiêu Tiểu Yến (nhieu_tieu_yen) lent her died in her hand she sang on, said it had flown, and watched Yến search the ridge a week.
people.appearance: A voice a head taller than she is.

ties.note: keeps a daily record of the birds' moods

people.backstory: Giải Vân Tiêu's (giai_van_tieu) disciple, who rides the post road to the vassals when the birds cannot fly and is learning seals. He reads over his master's shoulder, and when a letter went astray he gave Mã Tín Phi (ma_tin_phi) up to Giải Vân Tiêu's temper to save himself; Mã lost the Hà Loan run for a season.

people.role: Servant cage-maker, the only one the pavilion allows
people.backstory: A raft-village man with a Metal root who weaves the few training cages the pavilion permits. He made nine travelling cages for the head's gift this year, and when he was told not to ask what they were for, he charged double; Nhiêu Tiểu Yến (nhieu_tieu_yen) paid it from the loft's grub money and the red-crested nine ate thin for a month.
people.appearance: Walks as if the ground were a raft, swaying on dry land.

people.cause: fell from Triều Phượng Đỉnh at dawn, at 150 (N-bach_vu-02)
people.role: The old catcher who founded Bách Vũ Các with the Tạ sisters (1110) and refused to lead it
people.backstory: A bird catcher of the cinnamon woods who believed all birds bow to the phoenix (V137) and taught the two Tạ girls (ta_thanh_loan, ta_thanh_thuoc) a hundred calls. He would not be head. Every spring he climbed Triều Phượng Đỉnh, the Summit Where the Birds Pay Homage, to watch the dawn and see if they bowed. In 1160 he did not come down.

ties.note: keeper of the moulting lofts' feather rolls

people.cause: killed by the dark apes of Huyền Viên Lâm while netting

people.backstory: A Hà Loan netter who married Tạ Thanh Thước (ta_thanh_thuoc) and went into the dark ape forest once too often for its parrots in 1168.
